claim_label: SMA and Jamming Co-existence in Variable-Stiffness Structure
claim_text_original: SMA and jamming in the same variable-stiffness device is novel.
claim_text_normalized: Simultaneous integration of shape memory alloy (SMA) elements and jamming mechanisms within the same variable-stiffness robotic structure.
why_potentially_novel: At mentor proposal, integrating active SMA smart actuation with passive frictional jamming in a single structural member was thought to be an unprecedented multi-functional combination.
search_conducted: MP1-V001 core prior-art search across IEEE, RSJ, and JSME publications on SMA and jamming integration.

strongest_prior_art_threat.paper_title: Variable-Stiffness and Deformable Link Using Shape-Memory Material and Jamming Transition Phenomenon
strongest_prior_art_threat.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V001/2022-Variable-Stiffness and Deformable Link Using Shape-Memory Material and Jamming Transition Phenomenon.pdf
strongest_prior_art_threat.what_source_actually_proves: Demonstrates a soft robotic link co-integrating embedded NiTi SMA wires with vacuum granular jamming, enabling active shape restoration combined with tunable locking stiffness.
strongest_prior_art_threat.what_source_does_not_prove: NiTi wires serve as embedded actuation/recovery tendons, not as the mutual contacting and slipping jamming elements.

source_records.paper_title: Variable-Stiffness and Deformable Link Using Shape-Memory Material and Jamming Transition Phenomenon
source_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V001/2022-Variable-Stiffness and Deformable Link Using Shape-Memory Material and Jamming Transition Phenomenon.pdf
source_records.what_source_actually_proves: Co-existence of SMA wires and granular jamming in a variable-stiffness robotic link.
source_records.what_source_does_not_prove: Does not use NiTi wires as the jamming medium.

source_records.paper_title: Effect of R-phase on shape recovery speed of Ti-Ni shape memory alloy wire for variable-stiffness mechanism using jamming transition phenomenon
source_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V001/2024-Effect of R-phase on shape recovery speed of Ti-Ni shape memory alloy wire for variable-stiffness mechanism using jamming transition phenomenon.pdf
source_records.what_source_actually_proves: Characterizes R-phase transformation speed of Ti-Ni wires embedded inside a jamming transition link.
source_records.what_source_does_not_prove: Does not study inter-NiTi contact friction.

claim_before: SMA and jamming in the same variable-stiffness device is novel.
claim_after: Co-existence of SMA and jamming in the same device is established prior art; device-level integration novelty rejected.
reason_for_change: Takashima lineage (2022–2026) and Matsumoto et al. (2024) extensively published the co-integration of SMA wires and jamming transitions.
scientific_consequence: Must separate device-level co-existence (closed) from inter-wire contact mechanics (re-routed to C5/C7/T1).
feasibility_impact: Confirms practical feasibility of combining SMA and jamming, but bars whole-device novelty.
pivot_relevance: Key architectural pre-emption forcing the pivot to mechanics core in MP1-V001.
historical_interpretation: Closed at V001 (S04). Confirmed as robust closure at Stage 3 (S12) with explicit clarification separating SMA backbone from NiTi contact network.
superseded_interpretation: Belief that pairing an SMA element with a jamming element constituted a novel robotic architecture.
corrected_interpretation: Co-existence is well-established prior art; scientific interest only survives if NiTi wires themselves form the contact network.
